back_translation: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Sovereign Master seated on a throne, lofty and held in exaltation, and the train of His royal robe filled the temple.
Above Him stood seraphim, each one having six wings: with two wings he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with the other two he flew.
Each kept calling in response to the other: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory."
The voice of those calling made the foundations of the thresholds shake, and the temple was filled with smoke.
Then I cried out: "Woe to me! I am ruined, for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King — the LORD of Hosts."
Then one of the seraphim flew to me; in his hand was a red-hot burning coal, which he had taken with tongs from the altar.
He touched my mouth with that coal and said: "Behold, this has touched your lips; your iniquity has been taken away, and your sin has been atoned-and-cleansed."
Then I heard the royal voice of the Sovereign Master saying: "Whom shall I send? And who will go for us?" And I answered: "Here am I. Please send me!"
He said: "Go and tell this people: 'Listen and listen again, but do not understand; look and look again, but do not perceive.'

Make the heart of this people numb-calloused, make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes — lest they see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn back and be healed."
Then I asked: "O Sovereign Master, how much longer?" And He answered: "Until the cities are left ruined without inhabitant, the houses without people, and the land is left utterly desolate,
until the LORD has sent the people far away, and the abandoned places are many in the midst of the land.
And though a tenth part remains in the land, it will be burned again. Yet like a great oak or an oak that, when felled, still has its stump remaining — the holy seed is the stump of that land."
